findings.text: Upheld as a defect (question 2). Line 200 of the diff, `isFromTheHost(row.prompt) ? "" : withoutNotes(row.prompt, told)`, rewrites the first step of `prepareTexts` (src/distill/pipeline.ts:214) by hand instead of calling it. This is logic, not boilerplate: the rule that a host prompt is not the user speaking, and the notes removal. The proof's candidate ids and its metrics depend on this copy staying the same as the drain's, and nothing reports it if the two drift. Fix: export the pre-filter step from pipeline.ts and call it in both places.
Advisory (question 8). `noiseOf` and `NoisePattern` are exported, but nothing outside noise.ts uses them. The rubric calls an unused export advisory.
Advisory (question 8). `IMPORT_WORDING` and `IMPORT_JUDGE_VERSION` are exported, but only rejudge.ts uses them. The rubric calls an unused export advisory.
Advisory (question 6). `VERDICT` is the only `REPORT` pattern without the `/i` flag. This is a style difference, and a comment would make clear whether matching only uppercase is meant.
Advisory, debt. The literal 0.5 in `hasDurable` disagrees with `KNOWLEDGE_THRESHOLD` 0.45, but the diff did not write this line, so it is outside the change.

Dropped: no line named. The reviewer filed question 11 as not answerable, naming facts the spec rewrite removed but no line of the diff, and saying it could not tell whether they were dropped on purpose. A finding with no line cannot be upheld.

Upheld as a defect (question 1). AC-11 is a behaviour criterion (spec.md:29; recorded as red then green). Its red and green runs cover only the `toldInSession` bounds. No test fails if the proof stops working on a read-only copy (quality.sh:73) or stops using TypeSafe verdicts only (quality.ts:406-436). A typecheck cannot see either property. A smoke run against `WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_TYPESAFE_URL` could have asserted both.

Upheld as a defect (question 8). The fixtures at lines 107-108, `[arka:gate:4] W3b selada 41585f989 · memória fechada` and `[arka:routing] …`, are copied from the real labelled sample and name a real workspace's protocol tag. The rubric treats a real name in a fixture as a defect. A neutral tag such as `[crm:gate:4]` would test the same AC-9 behaviour.
Advisory (question 6). The test's name overstates what it proves, but the worth discount is proven by the test before it. The rubric calls a weak name advisory.
Advisory. No test pins the calibrated value 0.45. The behaviour of AC-3 (the title must be knowledge) fails on reversion, so question 1 is answered. A boundary case at 0.45 would pin the number.

Advisory. The drop names are asserted at the `dropNoise` level (noise.test.ts:172-186), so AC-1 has a test that fails on reversion. That `prepareTexts` passes the names on to the proof is not checked.

Advisory. Nothing ties a recording to the question wording it was made with. The question keys are checked, and the wording is covered by tests/unit/questions.test.ts, so AC-4 still fails on reversion. The comment at lines 84-85 claims more than the floors check.

Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The proof's output files are written with the default umask. The tool is for the operator only, the work dir is outside the repository and the live dirs, and the redacted text goes only to the user's own TypeSafe. Suggested hardening: `umask 077`.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. A work-dir path containing `'` would break the `.backup` argument. Only the operator supplies that path, so there is no untrusted caller.
Advisory, debt. The same pattern is in a file this diff did not touch.

Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The rollback is stated as a release, and the missed target on B is recorded and accepted (D-12, ADR 0023). No rollback or dependency is missing from the spec, so this is not a defect.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. Skips caused by the filter or by the policy cannot be told apart in the first hour after release. The spec names this as a known limit (line 299).

Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The code ships 0.45 while spec.md:14, the design and the plan still say 0.5, and the calibrated value is recorded only in ADR 0023. The reviewer did not raise it as a defect, and the rollback and dependencies are stated, so it stands as advisory.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The plan names no release step (no version bump, no `bun run plugins`). No line is given, and the reviewer did not raise it as a defect.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. Heuristic version 2 takes effect with no runtime switch back to version 1. This matches the rollback the spec states (a release).
Advisory, debt. The consolidation behaviour predates the change and the change does not alter it.
Advisory, debt. `compact` can remove the skipped turns a later cleanup would need, but this file is outside the diff.

Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The spec's §7 wording (lines 166 and 176) still gives the old `kind` question, but ADR 0023 records the calibrated change, so no boundary is crossed. Fix: update §7 or point it to the ADR.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The pipeline's public surface is wider than the `prepareTurn`/`draftTurn` seam the design names. This is a convention note, not drift.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. `toldInSession` still scans `injections`, as the old query did. The new conditions and their types are correct.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The `NOT EXISTS` subquery has no index to serve it, but it runs once per sample on the copy only, never on the live store or a hook path.

Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. Neither ADR 0023 nor the scripts say how long the work-dir files are kept or how to erase them. No column is involved, and the files sit outside the repository and the live dirs.
Advisory, as the reviewer filed it. The migrations run on the copy only. The live store is only read, and nothing in `measure` writes.
Advisory, debt. `injections` has no full index on `session_id`, and this file is outside the diff.
Advisory, debt. Noted only; this file is outside the diff and nothing in the diff needs more.
